# A. Warm-Up {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Yesterday the robot learned to **see**. Today it learns to **feel**. 🧱

## Where we left off

| Yesterday | What you own |
|---|---|
| 👀 **the eye, calibrated** | echo 0–100 · threshold per surface |
| 📈 **`error × KP`, third time** | `follow_line` rides the edge |
| 📐 **two eyes square up** | `square_on_line` at the junction |

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
🤔 The eye reads the **floor**, but what about a **wall**? And we carry no distance sensor…
:::

⏱️ **Time: 5 minutes, then robots out**

::: {.notes}
Recap by asking, not telling: "how does the robot know where it is?" Yesterday's answers all live on the floor — the calibrated eye, the P follower, the two-eye square. Today's problem stands upright: walls. We carry no distance sensor — and be accurate about why, because the easy answer is wrong. It is **not** that the ports ran out: port **A** is free on our robot (the stock kit is the thing with all six full). It is that a distance sensor would buy us nothing the wheels cannot already feel, and a stall is repeatable to the millimetre while an ultrasonic reading is not — so the spare port is better spent on a second eye, or on nothing. The cap that *does* bind us is the **4-motor** limit (§5.2.8), and it binds mechanisms, not sensors: F and B drive, E and C grip, and that is the four. That constraint is the day's gift — the drive motors themselves become touch sensors. Arc of the day: feel the wall (stall), back off a measured distance, wrap it in a patrol loop (yesterday's `if` now lives inside a `while`), then bottle `drive_to_wall` + `wall_square` into the library and read the 255 scoresheet the anchor-first way. Keep this slide to five minutes: per the W2 delivery rhythm (decision #22), robots are out by minute 15, so the recap is a springboard, not a lecture.
:::

## Before the wall: can it reverse? ↩️

Our first `drive_straight` only drove forward. Predict this call:

```{.python}
move.drive_straight(-50)  # back away by 50 mm?
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
The old finish line is **behind** the current wheel angle. Its `while angle < finish` check is False immediately, so it never drives.
:::
:::

Choose the direction with `if`. Measure distance travelled with `abs()`.

::: {.notes}
This is a required prerequisite, not a stretch. Run the old version once, predict the first check, then upgrade the function on the next slide. Both if and abs are familiar. Ten minutes including the forward/backward bench check.
:::

## A straight in either direction {.code-shrink}

```{.python}
def drive_straight(distance_mm, speed=400):
    if distance_mm < 0:
        direction = -1
    else:
        direction = 1
    start = left.angle()
    heading = hub.imu.heading()
    travel = abs(distance_mm) * DEG_PER_MM
    while abs(left.angle() - start) < travel:
        error = hub.imu.heading() - heading
        left.run(direction * abs(speed) - KP * error)
        right.run(direction * abs(speed) + KP * error)
        wait(5)
    left.stop(); right.stop()
```

Test `move.drive_straight(100)`, then `move.drive_straight(-100)`. A zero-distance call stays still.

::: {.notes}
Replace the forward-only definition in movements.py. The distance sign selects travel direction; speed is a magnitude. The wheel-angle difference measures progress from this call's start, without resetting the gyro or wheel counters. The gyro correction keeps the same signs in reverse: positive yaw still needs leftward correction. Check positive, negative and zero distances before approaching the wall. This upgrade is the code all later back-off calls use.
:::

# B. The Motor Is a Sensor {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

No distance sensor anywhere on this robot, and it already knows how to **feel**. 🧱

## Feel it: see the invisible 📉

```{.python}
# Wheels lifted first; the loop reads a motor already running.
left.run(150)
while True:
    print("wheel speed:", left.speed())
    wait(100)
```

🤖 **Robots out.** Run the loop and **grab the wheels**, and watch it dive. Then the wall board: same dive, no hand.

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .teal}
The speed dive **is** the wall, and every motor has **`stalled()`** and **`run_until_stalled()`**.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
"Make the invisible visible" — same habit as the gyro heading in Week 1, and this one happens on the real robot, not a slide (the animated version lives in the 🏠 appendix for home replay). Sequence: print loop running → student hand-blocks the wheels → speed crashes → then the same crash against the wall board. Only *after* they've seen the crash do you name the stall tools: `left.stalled()` asks "are you jammed *right now*?", `left.run_until_stalled()` is "roll until you jam" in one call. Point out why this beats an ultrasonic sensor even though port A is free and we could fit one: a touch via stall is repeatable to the millimetre and never lies about a wall it can "see through."
:::

## Fix it: stall = touch, then back off 🧱

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1|2|3-4|5|6|7"}
APPROACH_SPEED = 150         # deg/s, gentle, not a crash
right.run(APPROACH_SPEED)    # right rolls along…
left.run_until_stalled(APPROACH_SPEED,
                       duty_limit=50)   # …until LEFT jams
right.stop()
hub.speaker.beep()           # "I arrived"
move.drive_straight(-BACKOFF_MM)    # measured, repeatable
```

🤖 **Robots out.** Build it and tune `BACKOFF_MM` against the board. This is today's competition in seven lines.

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .purple}
Gentle touch · wait for the jam · back off a **measured** `BACKOFF_MM`.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Stress the gentleness knobs: a low approach speed (≈150 deg/s) and `duty_limit=50` — the duty limit caps how hard the motor is *allowed* to push, so the reading is crisp and the LEGO survives. Driving straight into a wall jams both wheels, so watching ONE motor is enough — `run_until_stalled` blocks on the left while the right just rolls. The negative-distance call uses the upgraded `drive_straight` that every student tested in today's warm-up. Ask which line selects reverse and which line measures the distance. Back-off is measured, not guessed — `BACKOFF_MM = 50` ends exactly 5 cm off the wall, every run. (The pro equivalent, `DriveBase.stalled()`, arrives with the D8 reveal.)
:::

# C. Patrol & React {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

One wall is a fluke. A real run is a **patrol**. 🔁

## Break it: the one-shot miss 😴

::: {.qbox}
[Your sense→act runs **once**. What happens at the **second** wall?]{.qtitle}
:::

🤖 **Robots out.** Run it, aim it at a second wall by hand. Nothing.

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .coral}
Your code was *right*. It just **stopped too soon**, and that's a **loop's** job.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Let them run the one-shot to death on the real robot: it handles wall 1 perfectly, then dies — perfection that only lasts one event. The point is emotional before it's technical: "your code was *right* — it just stopped too soon." Loops are not a new trick from scratch; they already met `while` and `for` on Day 3's square. Today those loops wrap a *sensed* decision instead of a fixed count of sides. (The animated one-shot-vs-patrol comparison lives in the 🏠 appendix.)
:::

## Name it: the patrol loop 🔁

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1|2|3|4-6|7|8|9-10"}
hub.imu.reset_heading(0)
for lap in range(PATROL_LAPS):          # counted repeat = laps
    left.run(PATROL_SPEED); right.run(PATROL_SPEED)
    while not left.stalled():           # repeat until the wall
        if left_eye.reflection() < THRESHOLD:
            hub.speaker.beep(880)       # react, don't stop
        wait(10)
    left.stop(); right.stop()
    move.drive_straight(-BACKOFF_MM)           # measured back-off
    move.turn(90 * (lap + 1), absolute=True)   # absolute appointment
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .teal}
Two loops **nested**: `for` counts laps, `while` waits for the wall, and the `if` reacts **on the move.**
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Read the shape aloud: outer `for` = "do this lap N times," inner `while not left.stalled()` = "keep rolling until you feel the wall," inner `if` = "and if you cross a staff line on the way, sing out" — yesterday's calibrated threshold, reused as-is. The `if` living *inside* the `while` is the subtle win — reaction happens continuously during motion, not as a stop-and-check. (That's also why this loop uses `left.stalled()` rather than the blocking `run_until_stalled` from this morning — the robot needs to keep *checking things* while it rolls.) `turn(90 * (lap + 1), absolute=True)` is the library day's absolute-appointment trick doing its job silently: corner 1 aims at 90, corner 2 at 180 — a bumped corner can't poison the next one. This program is the literal answer key for Gentle Giant's loop bonus. With one board and no table borders yet, patrol two "walls" by moving the board between reps or using a wall + heavy box pair — the loop doesn't care.
:::

# D. Bottle It: Two New Verbs {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

Bottle today's tricks into `movements.py`, then read the scoresheet like a pro. 📦

## `drive_to_wall` and `wall_square` join the library 📦 {.code-shrink}

```{.python code-line-numbers="|1-5|7-9|10-11|12|13|14"}
def drive_to_wall(speed=150):
    """Roll gently until the wheels feel the wall."""
    right.run(speed)
    left.run_until_stalled(speed, duty_limit=50)
    right.stop()

def wall_square(heading=0):
    """Press BOTH wheels flat on the wall → truth restored."""
    left.run(120); right.run(120)
    while not (left.stalled() and right.stalled()):
        wait(10)
    left.stop(); right.stop()
    hub.imu.reset_heading(heading)   # the wall never lies
    drive_straight(-BACKOFF_MM)
```

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
::: {.cardbox .purple}
Both wheels flat on the wall → heading **known again**. **The wall never lies.**
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Same promotion ritual as the library day: the morning's loose fix-it lines get names and move into `movements.py`, right under `drive_straight` and `turn`. Walk `wall_square` slowly. Its loop header is *Line King*'s `square_on_line` check with `stalled()` swapped in for the eye: ask the room to read `not (… and …)` aloud before explaining anything. It's the first verb whose *output* is trust, not motion: waiting for BOTH motors to stall means the bumper is flat on the wall, so the physical world just told you your heading exactly; `reset_heading(heading)` writes that truth back into the gyro, and the measured back-off leaves you at a known distance too. Gyro drift accumulates over a 2-minute run — squaring is how Weeks 3–4 missions reset it between tasks, which is why this humble verb outlives almost everything else. Demo: spin the robot a few times by hand (drift injected), wall_square, then a `turn(90, absolute=True)` — still true. Table note (decision #23): until the bordered table exists, `wall_square` trains on the fixed board; when the table lands we re-validate it at the true border positions — that's the table-arrival checkpoint.
:::

## Read the scoresheet: anchor first 🗺️

```{=html}
<div class="sim">
  <div class="sim-controls">
    <button class="sim-btn teal" data-sim="scStep">▶ build the score, layer by layer</button>
    <button class="sim-btn ghost small" data-sim="scReset">reset</button>
  </div>
  <svg width="820" height="150" viewBox="0 0 820 150">
    <rect class="board" x="30" y="46" width="760" height="46" rx="8"/>
    <!-- segments: scaled so 255 -> 760px, x start 30 -->
    <g id="scSegs"></g>
    <line x1="432.4" y1="34" x2="432.4" y2="104" stroke="#625D9C" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
    <text class="label purple" x="432.4" y="28" font-size="12" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">&#8776;135 &#183; the gate</text>
    <line x1="551.6" y1="104" x2="551.6" y2="120" stroke="#E96852" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
    <text class="label coral" x="551.6" y="134" font-size="12" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">&#8776;175 &#183; post-gate stretch</text>
    <text class="label" x="790" y="134" font-size="12" font-weight="800" text-anchor="end">255 max</text>
  </svg>
  <div id="scMsg" class="sim-msg">the anchor run scores <b>~135 with NO color sensor</b>, and that's what we build first.</div>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
  var X0=30, W=760, TOT=255, step=0;
  var segs=[
    {n:'Instruments', pts:45, c:'#00AE8D', tier:0},
    {n:'Cables',      pts:30, c:'#00C9A7', tier:0},
    {n:'Avoidance',   pts:40, c:'#625D9C', tier:0},
    {n:'Microphone',  pts:20, c:'#9B8EC0', tier:0},
    {n:'Fixed notes', pts:40, c:'#E96852', tier:1},
    {n:'Random notes',pts:80, c:'#FFB548', tier:2}
  ];
  var msgs=[
    'the anchor run scores <b>~135 with NO color sensor</b>, and that\'s what we build first.',
    '<b>Anchor ~135</b>: Instruments 45 · Cables 30 · Avoidance 40 · Microphone 20, zero color needed. 🧱',
    '<b>+40 fixed notes</b> (green/red) → <b>~175</b>: a post-gate stretch, taken only after the lock. 🎶',
    '<b>+80 randomized notes</b> → <b>255</b>: the Week-5 stretch. Anchor first, always. 🌈'
  ];
  function xw(pts){ return pts/TOT*W; }
  function render(){
    var html='', x=X0;
    // tier 0 shown at step>=1, tier1 at step>=2, tier2 at step>=3
    for(var i=0;i<segs.length;i++){
      var s=segs[i], w=xw(s.pts);
      var on = s.tier < step;
      html += '<rect x="'+x.toFixed(1)+'" y="46" width="'+(on?w:0).toFixed(1)+'" height="46" fill="'+s.c+'" opacity="'+(on?1:0)+'">'+
              '</rect>';
      if(on && w>34) html += '<text x="'+(x+w/2).toFixed(1)+'" y="75" font-size="12" fill="#fff" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">'+s.pts+'</text>';
      x += on ? w : 0;
    }
    SIM.html('scSegs', html);
    SIM.html('scMsg', msgs[Math.min(step,3)]);
  }
  SIM.def('scStep', function(){ if(step<3){ step++; render(); } });
  SIM.def('scReset', function(){ step=0; render(); });
  render();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.cardbox .teal}
**135 points, zero color.** Never trade a reliable anchor for a shaky full run.
:::

::: {.notes}
This slide connects the whole bootcamp to the scoresheet — and now the mat is physically in the room, point at the real zones while clicking through the tiers. The load-bearing idea: color is *risk* (lighting, calibration — they watched the numbers move between surfaces yesterday), so we defer every point that needs it. Everything the anchor needs lives color-free: the precise driving and wall verbs this week builds, then the Week-3 team mechanisms — cables, instruments, microphone, avoidance. Fixed notes (+40) are a **D24** stretch, taken only after the ×20 lock passes; the randomized notes (+80) leave the five weeks entirely and open the continuation season (decision #30). If a parent asks "why not go for 255 now?": the gated deliverable is the ~135 anchor landed 20 times at 90%+ (decision #30), and a reliable 135 beats a heroic 255 you land one time in ten — this is a WRO scoring truth, not a confidence thing.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
  var X0=50, X1=540, YB=165, TSPAN=3.2, VMAX=180, WALLX=150;
  var trace=SIM.trace('wsTrace');
  function yOf(v){ return YB - (v/VMAX)*(YB-25); }
  SIM.def('wsRun', function(){
    var t=0, v=0, botx=30, hit=false;
    trace.clear();
    SIM.set('wsFlag','opacity','0');
    SIM.tf('wsBot','translate(30,75)');
    SIM.loop('ws', {
      dt: 0.008,
      step: function(dt){
        if(botx < WALLX){ v += (150-v)*0.12; botx += v*0.02; }   // rolling toward the wall
        else { hit=true; v *= 0.72; }                            // wheels jammed → speed collapses
        t += dt;
        return (hit && v < 12) || t > TSPAN;
      },
      draw: function(){
        trace.push(X0+(t/TSPAN)*(X1-X0), yOf(v));
        SIM.tf('wsBot','translate('+(30 + (Math.min(botx,WALLX)/WALLX)*143).toFixed(1)+',75)');
      },
      done: function(){ if(hit) SIM.set('wsFlag','opacity','1'); }
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```

The same dive you saw on your real robot. The speed trace collapsing *is* the wall.

## 🏠 One-shot vs patrol (sim) 🔁

```{=html}
<div class="sim">
  <div class="sim-controls">
    <button class="sim-btn coral" data-sim="ptRun" data-sim-arg="once">▶ one-shot <code>if</code></button>
    <button class="sim-btn teal" data-sim="ptRun" data-sim-arg="loop">▶ patrol loop</button>
  </div>
  <svg class="panel" width="270" height="270" viewBox="0 0 360 360">
    <rect x="40" y="40" width="280" height="280" fill="none" stroke="#625D9C" stroke-width="8"/>
    <text id="ptW1" class="label dim" x="180" y="30" font-size="13" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">wall 1</text>
    <text id="ptW2" class="label dim" x="336" y="184" font-size="13" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(90 336 184)">wall 2</text>
    <text id="ptW3" class="label dim" x="180" y="344" font-size="13" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">wall 3</text>
    <text id="ptW4" class="label dim" x="24" y="184" font-size="13" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90 24 184)">wall 4</text>
    <polyline id="ptTrace" class="trace" points="" stroke="#00C9A7" stroke-width="3"/>
    <g id="ptBot" transform="translate(180,300)"><use href="#sim-bot-mini" transform="scale(0.55)"/></g>
    <text id="ptMsg" class="label" x="180" y="185" font-size="17" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle"></text>
  </svg>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
  var NOSE=16.5, LO=44, HI=316;      // wall inner edges; the nose leads by 16.5px
  var wallIds=['ptW1','ptW2','ptW3','ptW4'];
  var trace=SIM.trace('ptTrace');
  // corner heading pattern: start bottom-center facing up (-90)
  SIM.def('ptRun', function(mode){
    var laps = mode==='loop' ? 4 : 1;
    var x=180, y=300, h=-90;
    var leg=0, phase='drive';
    var prog=0, ended=false;
    SIM.set('ptTrace','stroke', mode==='loop' ? '#00C9A7' : '#E96852');
    trace.clear(); trace.push(180,300);
    SIM.text('ptMsg','');
    wallIds.forEach(function(id){ SIM.tone(id,'dim'); });
    SIM.loop('pt', {
      step: function(dt){
        var r=h*Math.PI/180, sp=150;
        if(phase==='drive'){
          x+=sp*Math.cos(r)*dt; y+=sp*Math.sin(r)*dt;
          var nx=x+Math.cos(r)*NOSE, ny=y+Math.sin(r)*NOSE;   // where the nose is
          if(nx<LO||nx>HI||ny<LO||ny>HI){                     // nose met a wall → stall
            if(nx<LO)x=LO+NOSE; if(nx>HI)x=HI-NOSE;
            if(ny<LO)y=LO+NOSE; if(ny>HI)y=HI-NOSE;
            SIM.tone(wallIds[leg],'coral'); phase='back'; prog=0;
          }
          trace.push(x,y);
        } else if(phase==='back'){
          x-=sp*Math.cos(r)*dt; y-=sp*Math.sin(r)*dt; prog+=sp*dt;
          trace.push(x,y);
          if(prog>=32){ leg++; phase='turn'; }
        } else if(phase==='turn'){
          if(leg>=laps){ ended=true; return true; }
          h+=90; phase='drive';
        }
        return false;
      },
      draw: function(){
        if(ended) return;
        SIM.tf('ptBot','translate('+x.toFixed(1)+','+y.toFixed(1)+') rotate('+(h+90).toFixed(1)+')');
      },
      done: function(){
        if(mode==='once'){ SIM.tone('ptMsg','coral'); SIM.text('ptMsg','program ended 💤 · walls 2–4 never happen'); }
        else { SIM.tone('ptMsg','teal'); SIM.text('ptMsg','4 walls patrolled ✓'); }
      }
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```

Your code was *right*. It just stopped too soon. Watch the loop keep the decision alive.

## 🏠 Gentle Giant practice (sim) 🐘

```{=html}
<div class="sim">
  <div class="sim-controls">
    <button class="sim-btn coral" data-sim="ggRun">▶ stall &amp; back off</button>
    <span class="sim-tag">BACKOFF_MM: <b><span id="ggV">50</span></b></span>
    <input type="range" min="0" max="110" step="1" value="50" data-sim-input="ggSet">
  </div>
  <svg width="820" height="150" viewBox="0 0 820 150">
    <rect class="ground" x="20" y="48" width="770" height="66" rx="10"/>
    <rect x="762" y="34" width="20" height="94" rx="4" fill="#625D9C"/>
    <text class="label purple" x="772" y="26" font-size="12" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">wall</text>
    <!-- 5 cm target zone: 50 mm before the wall. scale 4 px/mm -> 200px -->
    <line x1="562" y1="40" x2="562" y2="122" stroke="#00AE8D" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="6 5"/>
    <text class="label teal" x="562" y="140" font-size="12" font-weight="800" text-anchor="middle">5 cm mark 🎯</text>
    <g id="ggBot" transform="translate(60,81)"><use href="#sim-bot-mini" transform="rotate(90) scale(0.5)"/></g>
  </svg>
  <div id="ggMsg" class="sim-msg mono">set your back-off, then run. 50 mm lands you on the mark.</div>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
  var backoff=50;
  var WALLX=762, PXMM=4, NOSE=15;        // 4 px per mm; wall face at x=762; nose leads by 15px
  var touchX = WALLX - NOSE;             // nose touches wall
  SIM.def('ggSet', function(v){ backoff=parseInt(v,10); SIM.text('ggV', v); });
  SIM.def('ggRun', function(){
    var x=60, phase='fwd', bo=backoff;
    SIM.msg('ggMsg','rolling in…');
    SIM.loop('gg', {
      step: function(dt){
        if(phase==='fwd'){
          x += 320*dt;
          if(x>=touchX){ x=touchX; phase='stall'; SIM.msg('ggMsg','🧱 stalled, backing off '+bo+' mm'); }
        } else if(phase==='back'){
          x -= 260*dt;
          if(x <= touchX - bo*PXMM){ x=touchX - bo*PXMM; return true; }
        } else if(phase==='stall'){ phase='back'; }
        return false;
      },
      draw: function(){ SIM.tf('ggBot','translate('+x.toFixed(1)+',81) rotate(90)'); },
      done: function(){
        var gapMm = Math.round((WALLX - (x+NOSE))/PXMM);   // distance nose→wall
        var err = Math.abs(gapMm-50);
        if(err<=1){ SIM.msg('ggMsg','landed <b>'+gapMm+' mm</b> off the wall · bullseye on 5 cm 🎯','good'); }
        else { SIM.msg('ggMsg','landed <b>'+gapMm+' mm</b> off, <b>'+err+' mm</b> from the 5 cm mark. Re-tune BACKOFF_MM.','bad'); }
      }
    });
  });
})();
</script>
```

Replay today's competition. Slide `BACKOFF_MM` off 50 and watch the score suffer.
